rationale:
Evidence: iteration 10 (sensors at x = -0.025, -0.0125, 0, 0.0125, 0.025; sensor_size 0.016; kp 3.0; kd 0.8; ki 0; base_speed 0.9; line_loss last_direction) is the best raced design at 688.67, up from 686.99 at iteration 9. The oval finished 20 of 20 with progress 0.997 and steering_oscillation 0.17. S-bend finished 18 of 20 with mean time 2.56 s, inside the 3.0 s limit. Slalom progress was 0.562, flat against iteration 8 (0.563) and iteration 9 (0.532). Slalom still has 0 of 20 completions.

Decision: resubmit the iteration 10 design unchanged. This is the final iteration, so the design races on unseen tracks, not on another development track. Every tested lever has now been tried: gain (kp 3.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.6 to 0.8), sensing footprint (16 mm), spacing (narrowing from 0.04 steps to 0.025 steps), and speed (0.9). Slalom has stayed flat near 0.56 across the last three spacing and speed variants, so further single-variable steps are unlikely to convert slalom to completions. Each change also risks the s-bend and oval completions that carry most of the score. The approved, raced design is the safest choice for an unseen track of different shape.

Expected result: score close to the raced 688.7 on the development tracks. On the unseen track, the main risk is off-track ends on sharp bends, since the narrower array raises effective steering gain by about 1.33 times relative to the original 0.04 spacing. Hypotheses to check if the result is later visible: (a) the 18 of 20 s-bend completions hold on a different shape; (b) oscillation stays near 0.17 on the oval; (c) the unseen track's bends, if tighter than the s-bend, will show the off-track limit as the failure mode, not a stall.
